theme: Making the clock arrive everywhere at once
title: Variation-Aware Clock Tree: Buffer Insertion Under a Skew and Power Budget
strategies: trivial: type-0 (safe, low-variation) buffers only, fully closing every net's nominal-delay gap to the slowest net -- reproduces the checker's own reference construction; always feasible but power-wasteful

greedy: textbook zero-skew balancing -- fully close every net's nominal-delay gap to the slowest net using whichever buffer type needs the fewest extra insertions (the high-delay, high-variation 'turbo' type), regardless of the tight worst-case-skew budget

strong: exploit that the nominal-skew budget only requires PARTIAL closure -- raise each net only to the budget boundary (not to zero skew), using the low-variation 'safe' type, with a bounded fallback that keeps closing minimally with the same safe type if either budget is still missed
invalid: emits zero buffers on every net; since the nominal-skew budget is always strictly below the raw wire-delay spread, this is guaranteed infeasible
